meta.title: Mica, the native-feeling UI layer for Nuxt
meta.description: Native-feeling Vue components for Nuxt 4: light and dark themes, your brand colors, motion tuned for 60fps and docs your AI assistant can read. One line in nuxt.config.
meta.ogImageAlt: The mica. logo above the headline "Native calm, for every Nuxt app." and the nuxt.config extends line, next to a large blue dot.

hero.title: Native calm,
hero.lead: Mica is a UI layer of {n} components with light and dark themes, your brand colors and motion that holds 60 frames per second. Add one line to nuxt.config, no npm package needed, then write {tag}.
hero.stageLabel: A live sample of Mica components. Tilt follows your pointer.

sample.notifBody: mica-site is live on 3 regions in 41 s.

start.title: From one line to interface in a minute.
start.lead: Mica is a native Nuxt layer: there is no npm package to install, no plugin to register and nothing to import. Nuxt fetches it from GitHub. Components, theme tokens and composables are simply there.

components.title: {n} components. One steady hand.
components.lead: Every control shares the same type scale, radii, spacing and motion, so screens built months apart still feel like one product.

groups.Base: Type, icons, surfaces, logo and the theme switcher.
groups.Buttons: Actions, icon buttons, groups, menus and links.
groups.Controls: Switches, sliders, segments, chips and choices.
groups.Inputs: Fields, search, tags, codes, dates and forms.
groups.Navigation: Sidebars, tab bars, toolbars, steps and pagers.
groups.Feedback: Dialogs, sheets, toasts, menus and progress.
groups.Content: Cards, lists, tables, avatars and accordions.
groups.Charts: Lines, bars, rings, heatmaps and KPI tiles.
groups.Ai: Attachments, code blocks, questionnaires and agent traces.
groups.Chat: Messages, bubbles, markers and scrolling threads.

theming.title: Two colors in. A whole palette out.
theming.lead: Pick a primary and a secondary color. Mica derives hover states, soft tints, readable text shades and dark-mode variants, checks contrast, and remembers the choice without a flash on reload.

craft.title: The details you would have built yourself.
craft.motionTitle: Motion that never drops a frame
craft.motionBody: Springs written as CSS linear() curves, compositor-only properties and a frame probe in CI: p95 under 20 ms on mobile, tablet and desktop, light and dark.
craft.a11yBody: Keyboard paths, roving focus, ARIA roles, visible focus rings and reduced-motion fallbacks on every component.
craft.darkBody: Its own elevated surfaces and text shades, not an inverted light theme.
craft.ssrBody: Theme and brand colors are resolved on the server and in a tiny inline script.
craft.typedBody: Props, item shapes, emits and slot props are TypeScript types your editor completes.
craft.zeroBody: Vue, Nuxt and plain CSS. Nothing else ships to your users.

ai.title: Docs your AI assistant reads in 3k tokens.
ai.lead: Coding assistants should not have to parse {n} source files to place a button. Mica ships a compact index and one short file per component, generated from the sources and checked in CI.
ai.p1: Every component in one line, grouped, with the token cheat sheet.
ai.p2: Props, defaults, slots, emits and every named type, about 200 tokens each.
ai.p3: CI fails when a component changes and its docs do not.

showcase.title: Four products, built only with Mica.
showcase.lead: Complete, working screens. Open one, then switch the theme or the brand colors.

blocks.title: Blocks
blocks.lead: Ready-made application sections built only with Mica components: dashboards, tables, forms, chat, calendars, navigation and more. Every block adapts to its container, works in light and dark, and animates only transform and opacity.
